title: The Iterator Pipeline
goal: Source, adapters, one consumer. Every chain in this deck has that shape.

sections.text: An iterator pipeline has three parts. A source produces items, for example `.iter()` on a slice. Adapters transform the stream, for example `.map()` and `.filter()`. Exactly one consumer ends the chain and produces the final value, for example `.sum()`, `.collect()`, or `.next()`.

sections.caption: Nothing runs until the consumer asks.

sections.text: Iterators are lazy. Adapters do no work on their own; they only describe the transformation. The consumer pulls items through the chain one at a time. This is why order matters: `.filter().map()` and `.map().filter()` can both compile and produce different results.

Laziness also makes early exit free. A chain like `.filter(...).next()` stops at the first match and never looks at the rest of the data. The compiler turns these chains into the same machine code as a hand-written loop, so the choice is about clarity, not speed.
The puzzles in this deck are ordering puzzles: arrange source, adapters, and consumer so the pipeline says exactly what you mean.

explanation: A pipeline is source, adapters, and one consumer. Iterators are lazy: the consumer drives the work, and adapter order changes the result.
